notes: The RTL has mutually exclusive serial and barrel-shifter generate branches controlled by FAST_SHIFT_EN; the walks include the relevant branch-specific datapath blocks.
C4 lists shamt_i as an entry even though the serial count is also operation progress state; it is retained as fixed by CONCEPTS and treated as the input that initializes the coprocessor count.

points.reached by: rs1_i ==> barrel_shifter carries rs1_i into the barrel datapath at lines 122-123.
points.reason: The block computes and releases the operand-derived result through res_o, while valid_cmd can select zero data and suppress valid_o.

points.reached by: barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_core carries bs_level and bs_sign at lines 128-129.
points.reason: The generated stages select and construct shifted result bits, so tampering with their assignments corrupts the result, but the internal stage has no direct readout or blocking control.

points.reached by: barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_buf and barrel_shifter_core ==> barrel_shifter_buf carry bs_level to the registered result at line 138.
points.reason: bs_result stores the computed shifted word, so its assignment can corrupt the result and its clocked or reset update can prevent the result from becoming available.
The process loads and shifts sreg and controls its completion state, so altered datapath or completion assignments can corrupt or withhold the operand-derived result.

points.reached by: serial_shifter ==> res_o releases the serial result at line 111.
points.reason: res_o exposes sreg when done_ff is asserted, and the same completion gate can alter or withhold the returned result.
valid_cmd is the command-decode decision, and changing it can accept an unsupported shift or suppress a supported operation.

points.reached by: valid_cmd ==> barrel_shifter gates the barrel datapath at line 122.
points.reason: The decode decision selects whether the barrel path receives operand data and whether valid_o is asserted.

points.reached by: valid_cmd --> serial_shifter_core decides capture and busy assignments at lines 87 and 93.
points.reason: valid_cmd starts the serial operation and loads its state, so changing it can reject a valid command or start an unintended one.

points.reached by: shamt_i --> barrel_shifter_core selects barrel stages at lines 128-129.
points.reason: Each shift-amount bit selects whether its barrel stage shifts, so changing the input changes the returned shift distance.

points.reached by: shamt_i ==> serial_shifter_core loads shifter.cnt at line 94.
points.reason: The shift amount is loaded into and decremented as the serial step count, so changing it changes the number of shifts.

points.reached by: serial_shifter_core ==> serial_shifter carries shifter.cnt into run and done decisions at lines 108-109.
points.reason: The count-derived run and done decisions determine the serial operation's progress and valid signaling, so a modified count can produce an unintended shift behavior.
The process stores busy, done_ff and the step count, and altered assignments can abort, stall or falsely complete the serial operation.

points.reached by: serial_shifter_core ==> serial_shifter carries busy, count and completion state into valid signaling at line 110.
points.reason: The progress-derived valid_o signal reports completion, so changing run, done, busy or count decisions can falsely release or withhold the result.
